title: Rate-conservative dual-loop autoscaler with degradation contracts
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Implement a dual-loop autoscaling policy engine for Dedicated fleets that prioritizes throughput guarantees while enforcing conservative safety envelopes. The design separates a fast reactive inner loop (queue-length / latency control) from a slower predictive outer loop (demand forecast + contractual degradation). This ticket scopes the policy, configuration schema, safety checks, rollout plan and e2e validation criteria.

Motivation: Current autoscalers oscillate under spiky arrival patterns and occasionally breach per-tenant throughput targets or cause cascading latency SLO violations when burst capacity is consumed. We need a policy that is conservative about capacity churn, can honor per-tenant throughput SLAs, and supports explicit degradation contracts (what we allow to degrade first when capacity needs to be conserved).

Design highlights (technical):
- Inner loop (fast, reactive): continuous controller sampled every 2s that adjusts active replica concurrency and per-replica target throughput based on short windows (p50/p95 latency, queue depth). Behavior is rate-conservative: it will reduce target throughput when derivative of queue depth is positive and only increase throughput in small steps (slope limiter). Uses a PID-like controller with saturation and anti-windup.
- Outer loop (predictive, policy): runs every 30s and synthesizes demand forecasts using EWMA + short-window seasonality heuristics (30s/5m horizons). The outer loop sets target committed capacity (replica counts + reserved burst budget) subject to contractual limits and cost-smoothing. Forecast uncertainty is converted to a headroom requirement using configurable quantiles.
- Degradation contracts: per-tenant ordered list of allowable degradations (e.g., reduce max tokens, switch to quantized model variant, enable prefix-KV cache sharing, reduce max burst concurrency). Contracts include SL-recovery budget (how much degradation tolerated and for how long) and a cost-savings KPI. The outer loop can trigger degradations when forecasted demand + headroom would violate hard capacity caps.
- Safety limits and guards:
  - hard_capacity_cap: absolute max replicas for a fleet
  - slew_rate_limit: max fractional change in committed capacity per minute
  - min_reserved_for_sla: percent of fleet reserved for high-tier tenants
  - burst_budget_pool: finite credit pool consumed during bursts and replenished slowly
  - rollback_on_sla_violation: automatic rollback path that reverts outer-loop decisions if observed SLA regressions exceed thresholds for >2 consecutive measurement windows
- Tenant prioritization: policy supports weighted fair-share and a strict-priority fallback. Tenants can be annotated with customer_impact and contract_tier; outer loop uses these to allocate headroom and to order degradations.
- API/config schema: Add new policy type 'dual_loop_conservative' to autoscaling DSL with fields: inner_interval_s, outer_interval_s, forecast_quantile, max_slew_fraction_per_min, degradation_order, min_capacity_reserve_pct, burst_pool_size. Example: 
  policy: 
    type: dual_loop_conservative
    inner_interval_s: 2
    outer_interval_s: 30
    forecast_quantile: 0.85
    max_slew_fraction_per_min: 0.25
    degradation_order: ["reduce_max_tokens","switch_quantized","shrink_concurrency_per_replica"]
    min_capacity_reserve_pct: 12
    burst_pool_size: 2000

Telemetry & observability: Emit the following time-series and events: inner_target_throughput, outer_committed_replicas, forecast_quantile, chosen_degradations, burst_pool_balance, rollback_events. Add graph panels to the Dedicated Console route and a dedicated alert rule for unexpected rollback spikes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for inner-loop controller (stability, anti-windup) and outer-loop forecast utility (EWMA + quantile computation)
- Integration test in simulator showing fewer SLA breaches vs baseline under synthetic Poisson+burst workloads (target: reduce p95 SLA violations by >=40%)
- Feature flagged rollout with canary behavior and metrics dashboard PR linked
- Documentation: policy reference + example configs in docs site

Rollout plan: implement behind feature flag -> internal canary on low-risk fleet -> gradual enablement with metric gates (no increase in SLA breaches, bounded cost delta) -> GA in dedicated-2026.04.

Related artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/dual-loop-autoscaler-design, simulation notebooks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-dual-loop-sims, runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2398

Notes on tradeoffs:
- Conservative slew limits reduce oscillation but may increase short-term cost under sustained growth. This is an intentional product tradeoff (prioritize SLA stability over aggressive cost optimization).
- Forecasting simplicity (EWMA + heuristics) chosen to avoid model drift and operational complexity; we can iterate to ML-based forecasts once stable signals exist.

Security & compliance: No customer data leaves the control plane; degradation decisions are purely policy-driven. If tenants require audit entries for degradations, the policy will emit an immutable audit event to the tenant audit log (configurable).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit tests for controller behaviors and forecast quantile computation. 2) Simulator runs comparing baseline autoscaler vs dual-loop policy; p95 SLA violations reduced >=40% on synthetic bursty traffic. 3) Dashboard panels and alert rules added to Console. 4) Documentation and sample YAML in docs. 5) Feature-flagged rollout with canary gates (no >5% relative increase in p95 violations during canary).
